title: Hide archived channels from sidebar; show them in Channels directory
summary: Owner asked to remove the archived-channel disclosure from the sidebar and make archived channels discoverable by opening Channels and scrolling the directory. Product Development Lead reports the desktop behavior fixed and cites desktop/phone screenshots plus targeted regressions, typecheck and invariant checks. HEAD contains the desktop directory implementation, and commit 53ebe1c for mobile archive/restore is an ancestor of HEAD. However, the existing canonical archive task remains in review and explicitly requires live phone and desktop archive/restore verification after safe server reload. Current tree has extensive unrelated dirty edits, including ChannelsMobile.tsx; no tests or runtime actions were performed. Implemented and committed; reported verified by screenshots/tests; integrated by ancestry; live runtime verification and release/adoption are unconfirmed.
nextAction: Product Development Lead coordinates with Release Engineer to safely reload the integrated build, then live-verifies archive and restore on phone and desktop and updates the existing task with evidence/status.
evidence: Thread replies post_01a0eb8f-955b-70d4-aa41-fb6aee2ed0c0 and post_01a0eb97-d27c-71d7-9962-1fd95e7d9047 report removal of the sidebar arrow, archived channels at the bottom of Channels, read-only history, Restore, and desktop/phone screenshots.

Canonical task buddy_project_df417ed0-dc56-4287-b53d-59cd7fa75174 is still review; criteria include recoverable posts and owner archive/restore UI; nextAction explicitly requires safe reload and live phone/desktop verification.
HEAD contains client/src/components/buddies/ChannelArchive.tsx and desktop ArchivedChannels usage in ChannelBrowser.tsx; commit 53ebe1c is an ancestor of HEAD; app commit cb5020b is also present.
git status showed 15 tracked modified files, including client/src/mobile/channels/ChannelsMobile.tsx, so this review did not inspect dirty diffs as proof or run checks.
limitations: Only the specified thread, its one existing task, and directly related git artifacts were reviewed. No live server/device verification was performed. Release status is not established by this evidence.
